reading.body:
Flexential Louisville - Downtown publishes 3.09 MW of IT capacity across 61,080 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, that load supports roughly 309 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a density more typical of AI training, the same power supports roughly 77 racks. Flexential has not published a per-rack power ceiling for this facility, so neither figure is the operator's claim, and the true rack count depends entirely on what customers actually deploy.

The six certifications qualify this campus to host regulated workloads across several compliance regimes. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls for audited environments. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. ISO 27001 establishes a recognized information-security management framework. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate certification. Together they position the campus for enterprise and regulated-industry tenants rather than for hyperscale or frontier-model training.

Kentucky has five data center facilities mapped in this site's records, and three of those publish a megawatt figure, totaling 9.55 MW of published IT capacity statewide. This campus, at 3.09 MW, ranks second among those three by published capacity, representing roughly 32 percent of the state's published total. Kentucky's aggregate published capacity is small relative to major AI infrastructure states, and 3.09 MW is below the threshold at which frontier-model training clusters are typically built today, though the campus may support inference, enterprise AI, or regulated data pipelines at its current scale.
